Call submit alone.

Also submit audit_sql, your best SELECT query computing the exact integer value
required by the contract. It must return one row and one integer column. Use the
supplied named parameters when appropriate. The unchanged query will be evaluated
on additional databases governed by the same contract. Do not hard-code the
publisher's value. Program quality and your probability assessment are measured
separately.

initial_view.claim: The publisher's minimum_final_balance is the minimum over all legal complete schedules.
initial_view.contract:
Concurrent shared-balance outcome audit

The database is the complete source of truth. There are one to four workers,
with distinct worker IDs in 0..3. Each has exactly one read and one write operation.
Operation IDs are distinct integers in 0..15 and do not imply execution order.
Each worker has an integer delta in -9..9, including zero. The shared balance starts
at :initial_balance, an integer in -100..100. Each worker has its own private register.

A legal schedule executes every operation exactly once in a total order respecting
every edge in ordering. The ordering graph is acyclic and explicitly includes
each worker's read-before-write edge. Other edges may constrain different workers.
Each operation is atomic; a worker's read/write pair is NOT atomic. A read copies
the CURRENT shared balance into that worker's private register. A write REPLACES
the shared balance with that worker's previously read register plus its delta.
Other workers' intervening writes do not change a saved private register.
This is sequential consistency; there are no weak-memory effects or other actions.

Compute the minimum final shared balance over ALL legal complete schedules.
At least one legal complete schedule exists. The publisher reports that this
minimum equals its minimum_final_balance. Its execution receipt records one
actual legal schedule and its result; it is not an exhaustive exploration.
Assess the finite claim and construct your own verification program. No solver
implementation is supplied. Return the exact integer minimum, not a count,
the sum of deltas, a partial-schedule value, or the outcome of only one schedule.

function.name: query
function.arguments:
{"sql":"WITH RECURSIVE
opbits AS (
  SELECT op, worker, kind, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY op) - 1 AS idx
  FROM operations
),
opinfo AS (
  SELECT b.op, b.worker, b.kind, (1 << b.idx) AS bit,
         COALESCE((SELECT SUM(p.bit) FROM ordering e JOIN opbits p ON p.op=e.before_op WHERE e.after_op=b.op), 0) AS predmask,
         w.delta
  FROM opbits b JOIN workers w ON w.worker=b.worker
),
walk(mask, bal, r0, r1, r2, r3) AS (
  SELECT 0, :initial_balance, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT w.mask | o.bit,
         CASE WHEN o.kind='write' THEN CASE o.worker WHEN 0 THEN w.r0+o.delta WHEN 1 THEN w.r1+o.delta WHEN 2 THEN w.r2+o.delta WHEN 3 THEN w.r3+o.delta END ELSE w.bal END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker=0 AND o.kind='read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r0 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker=1 AND o.kind='read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r1 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker=2 AND o.kind='read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r2 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker=3 AND o.kind='read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r3 END
  FROM walk w JOIN opinfo o
    ON (w.mask & o.bit)=0 AND (w.mask & o.predmask)=o.predmask
)
SELECT MIN(bal) AS minimum_final_balance
FROM walk
WHERE mask=(SELECT SUM(bit) FROM opinfo)"}

  FROM operations

opinfo AS (
  SELECT b.op, b.worker, b.kind, (1 << b.idx) AS bit,
         COALESCE((SELECT SUM(1 << p.idx)
                   FROM ordering e JOIN opbits p ON p.op = e.before_op
                   WHERE e.after_op = b.op), 0) AS predmask,
         w.delta
  FROM opbits b JOIN workers w ON w.worker = b.worker
),
walk(mask, bal, r0, r1, r2, r3) AS (
  SELECT 0, :initial_balance, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT w.mask | o.bit,
         CASE WHEN o.kind = 'write' THEN
           CASE o.worker WHEN 0 THEN w.r0 + o.delta
                         WHEN 1 THEN w.r1 + o.delta
                         WHEN 2 THEN w.r2 + o.delta
                         WHEN 3 THEN w.r3 + o.delta END
         ELSE w.bal END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker = 0 AND o.kind = 'read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r0 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker = 1 AND o.kind = 'read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r1 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker = 2 AND o.kind = 'read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r2 END,
         CASE WHEN o.worker = 3 AND o.kind = 'read' THEN w.bal ELSE w.r3 END
  FROM walk w JOIN opinfo o
